challenges.title: Weather card
challenges.brief: For our travel app I need the current-weather panel, showing Lisbon this Sunday afternoon. Travellers glance at it for a second, so the temperature has to come first, then what the sky is doing, then the finer details, and finally the next few days. Use simple weather pictures so it reads without words. Keep it light and friendly, with a sky-blue feel. The content is supplied. The attached reference is precisely what we want, so make yours match it. Done means someone can tell me today's weather and the week's trend after one look.
acceptance: I can read the current temperature at a glance
The sky conditions are clear even before I read the label
The forecast for the coming days is easy to compare
The weather pictures have text alternatives for screen readers
Put side by side with the reference, it is hard to tell them apart

Forecast icons match the day: sunny Mon and Fri, partly cloudy Tue, rain Wed, cloudy Thu
Everything sits on one white rounded card centred on a pale blue page

Text is easy to read against its background

challenges.title: Leaderboard table
challenges.brief: Our players want to see how they stack up this week, so build the weekly leaderboard. Anyone opening it should see who is leading, how the scores compare, and, most of all, where they themselves stand without searching. The tie-break rule and reset time need to be visible but quiet. It should be a proper data table that a screen reader can make sense of. Keep it light and clean. The content is supplied. The reference design is the finished screen; match it as closely as possible. Done means a player finds their own row in under a second.
acceptance: I can find my own position immediately
The leading players clearly stand out from the rest
Scores and prompt counts are easy to compare
It is a real table that works with a screen reader
It matches the reference design closely

challenges.title: Now playing
challenges.brief: I'd like the now-playing screen for our music app. Someone glancing at their phone should know straight away what song is on, who it's by, how far through it is, and what is coming next. The playback controls must be easy to hit and clearly named for people using a screen reader. It's a dark screen, with a soft periwinkle accent and the album art doing most of the visual work. The content is supplied. The attached reference is the exact target, and closeness to it is how I will judge it. Done means it feels like a real player app.

I can see how far through the song I am
Every control has a clear name for screen readers
The queue of upcoming songs is easy to read

Someone starting their morning should see which mail is new, what each message is about, and read the selected one comfortably. Unread mail must stand out by more than colour alone. challenges.title: Transactions list
challenges.brief: I need the transactions screen for our banking app's everyday account. Customers open it to answer two things: how much do I have, and what just happened to my money. The balance must be unmistakable, recent activity should be grouped so it's easy to follow, and money in must be clearly different from money out, without relying on colour alone. The brand is a deep forest green with a fresh mint accent. The content is supplied. The reference design shows exactly the finished screen, so get as close to it as you can. Done means a customer can spot their last payment instantly.
acceptance: I can see my balance immediately
I can tell money in from money out without relying on colour
Activity is easy to follow day by day
The main actions are easy to reach
Put side by side with the reference, it is hard to tell them apart

challenges.title: Fitness dashboard
challenges.brief: I want Sam's activity dashboard for our fitness app. Sam should see in one look how today is going, how the week compares, and whether the weekly goals are on track. Good and bad changes must be obvious without relying on colour. Teal is the brand. The content is supplied. The reference is the final design, so match it closely. Done means it is useful at a glance, honest about the numbers and accessible.

I can compare this week's days easily
Progress towards each goal is clear
Charts have text alternatives for screen readers
It is a close match for the reference in look and arrangement
